findings.problem: Shell leakage: file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, logging (println), and domain construction are fused in a single function. Data/Calculations/Actions boundary is violated.
findings.failure_mode: Core logic depends on filesystem availability and stdout; cannot be tested deterministically or composed in pure pipelines. Side effects are invisible to the caller.
findings.fix: Split into three layers: (1) Actions: fn load_raw(path: &str) -> Result<String, IoError>, (2) Calculations: fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>, (3) Data: Record struct with smart constructor. Caller composes them.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - panic surface on I/O failure (file not found, permission denied, encoding error).
findings.failure_mode: Entire program aborts with panic when the file is missing or unreadable instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, FrameLoadError> with an IoError variant. Replace .unwrap() with ? operator: `let text = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| FrameLoadError::Io(e))?;`.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - panic surface on non-numeric or out-of-range value in any line's second field.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV input (e.g., empty file, line with missing field, non-numeric value like 'abc') causes a panic instead of a typed parse error. Partial data is silently lost.
findings.fix: Replace with fallible parse: `let val = parts[1].trim().parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| FrameLoadError::InvalidValue(parts[0].clone()))?;` and return Result<Vec<Record>, FrameLoadError>.

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked indexing into split result. If a line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields, this panics at runtime.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV line (e.g., single-field line, empty line) causes panic via index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed error.
findings.fix: Use .get(0).ok_or(FrameLoadError::MissingField(...)) and .get(1).ok_or(FrameLoadError::MissingField(...)) with typed error, or restructure with split_once.

findings.problem: (...) as u16 - lossy cast from u32 parse result to u16. Values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value like 70000 silently becomes 4464 (70000 - 65536), producing incorrect domain data with no error signal. Data corruption is silent and undetectable at parse time.
findings.fix: Parse directly to u16: `parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| FrameLoadError::InvalidValue(...))?`, or use `u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| FrameLoadError::ValueOutOfRange(...))?`.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line. Uses split instead of split_once. Also parts[0] and parts[1] access via indexing rather than destructuring.
findings.failure_mode: Every input line allocates a temporary Vec plus trimmed String allocations. No upper bound on lines loaded. split produces more elements than needed, and the Vec is only used for 2 field accesses.
findings.fix: Use `let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(FrameLoadError::MissingField(...))?;` with `value_str.trim().parse::<u16>()` for zero-allocation per-line parsing. Add a domain cap on total records with try_reserve.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) - I/O side effect (stdout) embedded in data-parsing logic. Also uses unchecked parts[0] indexing.
findings.failure_mode: Parsing function has observable side effects that cannot be suppressed in testing or production. Output ordering depends on input order, making deterministic testing impossible. stdout buffering can cause performance issues.
findings.fix: Remove println entirely from the parsing path. If logging is needed, use a callback/result enum variant that the shell layer decides how to handle (log, discard, or collect into a progress struct).

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, u16) used directly in the Record struct with no smart constructor. No parse boundary enforcement means callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Any code can create Record { name: "".to_string(), value: 0 } or Record with a name exceeding reasonable bounds. The name field accepts arbitrary strings including empty or whitespace-only values. The value field accepts any u16 including sentinel values that may be invalid in context.
findings.fix: Add a private constructor: impl Record { pub fn new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Self, RecordError> { ... } } with validation (non-empty name, value range). Make fields private or use a newtype for name.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence for load_frames. No bounded capacity limit on total records loaded. No try_reserve or domain cap.
findings.failure_mode: Loading a file with millions of lines will allocate unbounded memory, potentially causing OOM. No allocation budget exists for production use with untrusted input sizes.
findings.fix: Add a max_records parameter, validate input size, call Vec::new().try_reserve(max_records).map_err(|_| FrameLoadError::Allocation)?, and enforce the cap during iteration. Add benchmark evidence showing allocation behavior at scale.

findings.problem: No typed error type. Function returns Vec<Record> with panics as the only error signal. No error taxonomy for I/O, parse, validation, or allocation failures.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish between file-not-found, malformed data, out-of-range values, or resource exhaustion. Error handling is binary: success or panic.
findings.fix: Define: pub enum FrameLoadError { Io(std::io::Error), MissingField(usize), InvalidValue(String), ValueOutOfRange { field: String, value: String }, Allocation }, pub fn load_frames(path: &str, max_records: usize) -> Result<Vec<Record>, FrameLoadError>.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_frames allocation/throughput behavior
no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis
no allocation tracking (no try_reserve, no Vec::with_capacity, no domain cap)
no second-ring evidence (no clippy, no test suite, no command output)
no command-truth evidence - no verification commands were run
residual_risk: Static review only. Every function in the crate violates absolute laws: hidden I/O (fs::read, println), panic surfaces (2x unwrap), unchecked indexing, lossy cast, intermediate allocations, no error taxonomy, no parse boundary, no bounds, no benchmarks. Delivery is blocked until all violations are remediated.
